entry.title: Paul Reed Smith Inducted into Guitar Center’s Rockwalk at Eric Clapton’s Crossroads Festival

media:group.media:title: Paul Reed Smith Inducted into Guitar Center’s Rockwalk at Eric Clapton’s Crossroads Festival
media:group.media:description:
On Sept. 26, 2026, Guitar Center welcomed Paul Reed Smith into the Guitar Center Rockwalk during Eric Clapton’s Crossroads Guitar Festival in Austin, Texas.
Since 1985, the Guitar Center Rockwalk has honored more than 150 artists and music industry icons, immortalizing their handprints and signatures outside Guitar Center’s flagship Hollywood store. Smith now joins a lineage that includes Leo Fender, Les Paul, Ernie Ball, Jim Marshall and his friend and mentor Ted McCarty.
John Mayer delivered the induction remarks for Smith, celebrating the love of guitar that connects them and generations of players. Their friendship and creative collaboration—which includes the PRS Silver Sky—made Mayer’s role in the ceremony especially fitting.
In this video:
• Discover what Mayer says all guitarists share • Learn what Smith loves more than guitars • Find out what Dalporto did for Smith that never happened to the legendary guitar designer before • See Smith’s hands immortalized in cement for Guitar Center’s Rockwalk

entry.title: Eric Clapton on His Guitars, Music and the Meaning of Crossroads

media:group.media:title: Eric Clapton on His Guitars, Music and the Meaning of Crossroads
media:group.media:description:
Eric Clapton has owned and played some extraordinary guitars, but his attachment to them goes well beyond their history or collectibility. To Clapton, they’re “sacred things,” instruments that can provide inspiration, relief and a way through difficult moments.
Clapton talks about that bond, the Cream-era Gibson ES-335 that became “the star of the show” at the 2004 Christie's Crossroads auction and why supporting Crossroads remains inseparable from his own commitment to sobriety.

entry.title: From Motown to Doom Metal With One Bass Combo | Ashdown UK-SBM Bass Combo Demo with Pete Griffin

media:group.media:title: From Motown to Doom Metal With One Bass Combo | Ashdown UK-SBM Bass Combo Demo with Pete Griffin
media:group.media:description:
Pete Griffin (Dethklok, Zappa Plays Zappa and Generation Axe with Steve Vai, Zakk Wylde, Yngwie Malmsteen, Nuno Bettencourt and Tosin Abasi) explores the Ashdown SBM Combo Series, demonstrating how these lightweight UK-built bass combos deliver everything from vintage Motown warmth and contemporary slap tones to tube-inspired overdrive and full-on distortion.
“The first thing I would do with the SBM Combo is the same thing I would do with any Ashdown amp to get a great sound—nothing,” says Griffin. “You literally put everything straight-up flat, plug in and count off the song. It sounds that good. A lot of that is due to the Pre-Shape button, which gives you a nice contour to the sound without overly coloring it. Then, you can tweak it further.”
In this video: • Hear how the SBM Combo Series delivers vintage, modern, funk and metal bass tones with simple EQ adjustments • Discover how the footswitchable Drive control transforms a lightweight Class D combo into a tube-inspired powerhouse • Learn why Pete Griffin says the Pre-Shape circuit makes it easy to dial in a great bass tone right away • Find out why the UK-built SBM combos have become his favorite lightweight alternative to traditional tube rigs

entry.title: Pete Griffin Shows How a Few EQ Moves Can Transform Your Bass Tone | Ashdown OBM-300 Amp Head

media:group.media:title: Pete Griffin Shows How a Few EQ Moves Can Transform Your Bass Tone | Ashdown OBM-300 Amp Head
media:group.media:description:
Pete Griffin (Dethklok, Zappa Plays Zappa and Generation Axe with Steve Vai, Zakk Wylde, Yngwie Malmsteen, Nuno Bettencourt and Tosin Abasi) demonstrates the Ashdown OBM-300 bass head paired with the RBM-112T cabinet, showing how its intuitive 5-band EQ, Pre-Shape control and effects loop make it easy to dial in everything from vintage P-Bass warmth to more contemporary cutting bass tones.
"On top of Ashdown’s classic Pre-Shape switch, the OBM-300 adds a 5-band EQ, so you can really get the sound you're looking for,” says Griffin. “You can either add or subtract some of those high mids or the low mids to clear out some space for low-toned guitars or a kick drum, or you can crank it to dominate some of those frequencies a little bit more if that's what you're going for.”
In this video: • Hear how the OBM-300's five-band EQ shapes vintage, modern and mid-forward bass tones with just a few adjustments • Discover why Pete Griffin says the VU meter is one of Ashdown's most useful—and coolest—features • Learn how the effects loop helps preserve your fundamental bass tone while using chorus and other effects • Find out why Griffin relies on Ashdown amps for everything from Dethklok to Frank Zappa's music

entry.title: Drum-Off, Warped Tour and Building Guitar Center's Future | Inside the Noise (S3, E10)

media:group.media:title: Drum-Off, Warped Tour and Building Guitar Center's Future | Inside the Noise (S3, E10)
media:group.media:description:
Guitar Center Senior Manager of Content Max Lauer-Bader joins the company’s CEO Gabe Dalporto to reflect on the biggest moments from Inside the Noise Season 3, including the return of Drum-Off and conversations with artists such as Kevin Lyman, Stephen Perkins, Jimmy Eat World, Dave Kushner and others. Dalporto also shares how these interactions with artists are helping to shape Guitar Center's future—from creating better in-store experiences and supporting emerging musicians to building stronger creative communities for players.
"It's not just, 'I'm going to sell you an instrument,'" says Dalporto. "It's how do we help and support you at each stage of your musical journey?"

entry.title: Pete Griffin Demos the Ashdown PBM-200 "Ant" Bass Head & RBM-112T Cabinet

media:group.media:title: Pete Griffin Demos the Ashdown PBM-200 "Ant" Bass Head & RBM-112T Cabinet
media:group.media:description:
Pete Griffin (Dethklok, Zappa Plays Zappa and Generation Axe with Steve Vai, Zakk Wylde, Yngwie Malmsteen, Nuno Bettencourt and Tosin Abasi) demonstrates the Ashdown PBM-200 "Ant" bass head and RBM-112T cabinet, showing how this compact rig delivers power, clarity and versatility. Hear Griffin dial in everything from modern metal, slap bass and old-school R&B to effects-driven solo tones.
“It's really cool to see these guys are now making these smaller, lightweight pocket amps,” says Griffin. “Now that everybody brings modelers with them anyway, a lot of times I have my tone with my pedalboard—not necessarily with the amp—because people don't want to see amps on stage anymore, unfortunately, or travel with all that stuff. So, it really makes sense to have something this tiny that still gets nice and loud and delivers the sound that you want.”
In this video: • Discover why Griffin says the PBM-200 "Ant" is perfect for today's modeler-based live rigs • Hear how the Pre-Shape circuit creates a mix-ready bass tone with the push of a button • Listen as Griffin dials a bunch of different and useful low-end sounds • Learn why the lightweight PBM-200 head and RBM-112T cabinet deliver far more power than their size suggests
